text:
mia: Heads-up: we need a lightweight battlecard and a short launch post for the benchmark webinar next week. Goal: equip AEs with a 60s pitch and a one-page rebuttal vs clouds / LLM APIs / infra vendors.
calvin: Got it. I can draft the 60s pitch. Key bullets: transparent unit economics, predictable latency, deployment flexibility.
rachel: Research note: our tests show consistent tail-latency improvements when routing + cache are enabled. Worth calling out "tail stability" in the pitch.
devon_pm: For the launch post, we should avoid absolute claims. Propose structure: hook (real customer scenario), topline observation (percent range), methodology snapshot, CTA.
pat_sales: Sales ask: add two quick rebuttals for each competitor bucket. e.g., vs Cloud AI: "opaque pricing -> we show token-level cost breakdowns"; vs LLM APIs: "model drift risk -> rollouts + pinned versions"; vs Infra: "ops burden -> turnkey routing and autoscaling."
bench-bot: bench report: https://files.redwood/bench/1990011222/summary.pdf (includes sampling details)
mia: Good. Devon, can you draft the methodology blurb? Keep it 2 lines.
devon_pm: Sure: "Methodology: end-to-end app trace replay using 10k sessions (mix of 1-64 tokens), 8k token long tail tests, batching config X, prefix cache on/off. Comparisons against public managed endpoints with default batching."
calvin: For the AE 60s pitch: "Redwood gives predictable throughput and transparent unit costs so you can forecast ML spend. We match cloud simplicity with control and enterprise SLAs."
pat_sales: Short objection play: customer: "Why not just use cloud provider endpoints?" reply: "Cloud endpoints are easy, but opaque. We show per-route token spend, and route lower-cost variants when appropriate so your bill is predictable."
rachel: Also prepare an evidence card: two rows: cost (sustained load), latency (95th). Include sample numbers but mark as "observed in internal lab".
mia: Let's add a one-pager ops recipe for routing rules. Example snippet for CRM tag: ```{ "utm_source":"benchmark-webinar", "interest":"dedicated_or_trial", "lead_score":85 }```
ops-bot: suggested routing: if lead_score>80 and company_tier==enterprise -> AE_queue; else -> SDR_queue. (auto:ops-note)
devon_pm: Webinar CTA ladder: 1) spin up trial (credit), 2) schedule capacity consult, 3) request a tailored benchmark (SE-run). Map pages and forms.
pat_sales: Can we get a 1-paragraph microscript for SDR outreach? quick template: "Saw you joined our benchmark webinar — curious about predictable ML spend? 15m demo?"
calvin: I'll produce the post headline options: "How we cut token costs in steady-state inference" or "Making inference costs predictable at scale". Prefer shorter.
mia: Tone check: keep it factual, production-first, avoid hype words like "revolutionary". We need legal to sign off on numbers.
bench-bot: flag: sample sizes for 8k token runs = 120 per config. Recommend increase to 250 for public claim.
rachel: Agree. If we can't increase sample size before launch, use language: "in internal tests" and avoid precise %s.
devon_pm: I'll draft the battlecard layout: top: quick facts, middle: competitor buckets + rebuttals, bottom: AE plays and demo hooks.
pat_sales: Request: include 2 quick screens for the product demo: 1) cost breakdown dashboard, 2) route policy editor. Both are compelling.
ops-bot: Action created: MARKETING-1990-ROUTING-SPEC assigned to ops. Deadline: +5 days.
mia: OK owners: calvin = AE pitch + post headlines, devon = methodology + battlecard skeleton, rachel + bench-bot = numbers vetting, pat_sales = rebut bullets + demo scripts, ops-bot = routing PR. I'll consolidate and share a draft in #marketing tomorrow.
pat_sales: Can we run a 15-min roleplay with 3 AEs after draft? quick feedback for messaging tweaks.
calvin: I'll schedule.
mia: Thanks team. Final note: include a small FAQ entry on model upgrades and fallbacks: "We pin model versions for production, and can route to compatible variants if a new update is pushed." Keep it 1-2 lines.
bench-bot: reminder: weekly bench refresh Friday 09:00.
mia: Great. If no blockers, I'll publish the deck to the shared drive and tag reviewers. :sparkles:
